newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sydkraft says sees '97 profit 5 bln Skr.
newsitem.headline: Sydkraft says sees '97 profit 5 bln Skr.

text.p: Swedish power group Sydkraft said on Friday it expected to double its profit after financial items to more than five billion crowns for the full year 1997, from 2.5 billion crowns in 1996.

Sydkraft expected 1997 net sales to rise to close to 15 billion crowns from 13.6 billion crowns a year earlier and saw earnings per share climbing to 19.30 crowns from 9.52 crowns, it said in its first quarter earnings statement.

The forecast corresponded to a return on average capital employed before tax of 18.2 percent, compared to 11.7 percent in 1996, and on average capital employed after tax of 20.3 percent, compared to 11.8 percent, the company said.
Sydkraft posted a first quarter profit after financial items of 3.40 billion crowns, including a capital gain of 2.3 billion crowns from the sale of shares in German utility VEBA.
Net sales rose five percent to 4.36 billion crowns in the first three months of the year, while operating profit jumped 19 percent to 1.43 billion crowns.

"The result improvement stems mainly from larger hydro electric power production, from the acquisition of Orebro Energi and from the acquisition of shares in associates Graningeverken and Hamburgische Electricitats-Werke (HEW)," it said.
But net financial items were hurt by interest rate and currency effects in connection with the financing of the acquisitions, Sydkraft said.
Excluding the capital gain, the charge for net financial items widened to 326 million crowns from 222 million.
The acquisitions of shares in Orebro Energi and HEW also boosted total first quarter investments to 6.05 billion crowns from 267 million.
All business areas, apart from services, posted stronger first quarter sales.
